summary: Read a non-empty text in which every character is a digit. The code records A as 1, B as 2, and continues through the alphabet until Z is recorded as 26. Count how many legal readings the digit text has, and write that count. A lone 0 does not stand for any letter. Two neighboring digits form a letter only when the number they make lies from 10 through 26, ends included. A reading may mix pieces of one digit and pieces of two digits, and every different cutting counts. When no legal cutting exists, write 0.
notes: Compare after trimming trailing newlines. The input is one token of text without spaces.
